_meta.description: Data behind the acceleration chart in the Scalable Governance hero. Every number shown on the page resolves to an entry here. See data/VERIFICATION.md.
_meta.display: All five lines share one time axis, 1 Jan 2021 to 1 Jan 2027. The y-axis shows the selected measure in its own units (ticks per measure); the other four are drawn in grey on their own scales, for timing only.

capability.label: Capability
capability.measure: Length of software tasks (in human expert time) that frontier AI agents complete with 50% success

headline.basis: METR doubling time for frontier models released from 2023 on: 129 days (≈4.2 months), range 104–158 days. METR excludes points with central estimate above 16 hours from this fit.

capability.caption: Since 2023, the length of software tasks that frontier AI agents complete with 50% success has doubled about every four months (range 3.4–5.2 months). Points are the frontier models METR measured; estimates above 16 hours are left out because METR flags them as unreliable.

source.title: METR, Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models (Time Horizon 1.1), benchmark_results_1_1.yaml
source.licence: © METR, all rights reserved. Numbers cited; chart drawn by Scalable Governance.
source.note: Estimates above 16 hours are left out, as METR flags them as unreliable.

compute.label: Compute
compute.measure: Computing power of AI chips sold since 2022, all major designers combined (million H100-equivalents, cumulative)

headline.text: 3.4× more AI computing power each year
headline.basis: Epoch AI Trends: the computing power of the total stock of AI chips has grown 3.4× per year since 2022 (90% CI 3.2× to 3.7×; doubling every 6.8 months).

compute.caption: The AI chips sold since 2022 add up to about 31.6 million H100-equivalents by mid-2026, and this stock has grown about 3.4× per year. The figure combines Nvidia, Google, Amazon, AMD, Huawei and Cambricon; chips that have been retired are not subtracted.

source.title: Epoch AI, Data on AI chip sales (timelines by chip)
source.licence: CC BY 4.0. Cumulative totals are our sum of Epoch's quarterly median estimates across chips, as in Epoch's own cumulative view.
source.short: Epoch AI, Data on AI chip sales
source.note: Cumulative totals are our sum of Epoch's quarterly median estimates across chips; retired chips are not subtracted.

secondary_stat.basis: Epoch AI Trends: compute stock growth 3.4×/year, 90% CI 3.2× to 3.7×, since 2022.

cost.label: Cost
cost.measure: How many times cheaper it is to score 75% on PhD-level science questions (GPQA Diamond) than in January 2025, using the cheapest model available; Epoch's first cost per question divided by each later one
cost.axis_label: Times cheaper than Jan 2025 (score of 75% on PhD-level questions)

headline.basis: Epoch AI's lowest cost per question to score 75% on GPQA Diamond: $0.2989 (31 Jan 2025) divided by $0.000412 (9 Jul 2026).

cost.caption: GPQA Diamond is a multiple-choice exam of PhD-level science questions. With the cheapest available model, a score of 75% (counted up from the 25% guessing rate) cost 30 cents per question in January 2025 and 0.04 cents in July 2026. Across five benchmarks, Epoch AI finds costs falling about 13× per year since 2023.

source.title: Epoch AI, The plunging price of thought (Emberson & Roodman, 22 Sep 2026)
source.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Epoch AI publication). Modified: shown as times cheaper than the first point (Epoch's first cost per question divided by each later one). The linked code/data repository carries no licence file.
source.short: Epoch AI, The plunging price of thought (2026)
source.note: Shown as times cheaper than the first point: Epoch's first cost per question divided by each later one.

adoption.label: Adoption
adoption.measure: EU enterprises (10+ employees) using at least one AI technology (%)

headline.basis: Eurostat isoc_eb_ai, E_AI_TANY, EU27_2020, 10+ persons employed, 2021 and 2025.

adoption.caption: The share of EU enterprises with 10 or more employees using AI rose from 7.7% in 2021 to 20.0% in 2025. Larger firms use it more: in 2025, 17.0% of small, 30.4% of medium and 55.0% of large enterprises. No EU AI figures for 2022; the 2025 list of AI technologies adds image, video and audio generation.

source.title: Eurostat, Artificial intelligence by size class of enterprise (isoc_eb_ai)
source.licence: © European Union, reuse authorised with acknowledgement of the source (Commission Decision 2011/833/EU). Values rounded to one decimal in display.

points.label: EU, 2025
points.note: 2025 list of AI technologies adds 'generating pictures, videos, sound/audio'.

incidents.label: Incidents
incidents.measure: AI incidents recorded in the AI Incident Database, by incident year

headline.basis: Count of incidents.csv rows with a 2025 incident date in AIID snapshot backup-20261012101643 (12 Oct 2026).

incidents.caption: AI incidents with a 2025 incident date recorded in the AI Incident Database rose to 457, from 309 in 2024. These are reported incidents: counts reflect media attention and curation as well as occurrence, and past years are revised as incidents are added (snapshot of 12 Oct 2026).
